system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is only the requested medium noun phrase, excluding treatments; if none, leave it empty. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

input.intent: animate this photo: bring it to life with slow drifting motion
input.observed_phrase: Photorealistic cinematic concept-art/character reference sheet with a dark, moody, tactical neo-noir look, low-key cinematic lighting: cool blue-gray ambient night light and wet-surface reflections in the hero panel; soft directional studio light on the figure in the reference panels

card.summary: A cinematic character reference sheet for a person in black tactical clothing, featuring a rainy nighttime hero shot, front/side/back turnaround views, and close-up details of the face, jacket collar, hands, and boots.

subjects.descriptor: The same person appears throughout the reference sheet: an adult with short shaved sides and dark hair tied into a small topknot.
attributes: short, closely cropped hair at the sides
dark hair gathered into a small topknot at the back
black high-collared tactical jacket with straps and buckles
visible small scar or mark through an eyebrow
pose: standing in the hero shot with arms at sides and head turned toward the viewer's left
standing facing the camera in the front view
standing in a side profile facing the viewer's left
standing with back to the camera in the back view
neutral, serious expression in the face close-up
hands shown in a detail view with relaxed, slightly curled fingers

card.environment: Rainy nighttime urban rooftop or elevated walkway with metal railings and blurred city lights in the hero panel; plain dark studio background in the turnaround and detail panels.
card.lighting: Low-key cinematic lighting: cool blue-gray ambient night light and wet-surface reflections in the hero panel; soft directional studio light on the figure in the reference panels.
card.framing: Character reference sheet layout with a large full-body hero image, three full-body turnaround panels, and four cropped detail panels.
card.style: Photorealistic cinematic concept-art/character reference sheet with a dark, moody, tactical neo-noir look.

rendering_permission.reasoning: The caller expressly asks to animate the photo and specifies the desired slow drifting motion, which is an authorizing rendering transformation rather than a request to preserve the reference rendering.
